area: Bids (make orders): fills, speed, pick-off, why the rest did not fill, bids vs takers, and whether to run them at the current settings
trust_notes: What can be trusted: the 17 fills are real executed orders with their own closes and results; counts (3128 posted, 3082 ended unfilled, end reasons, 119.8 bid-hours and 16 fills in the last 24 h) come from the app's own totals. What cannot: (1) 17 fills in 6 games (7 in one game, 3 in another), all but 3 from before the focus tag existed (no sharp book for 11, kinds and margins since changed); QUICK_LIKELY (the current setting) has 0 fills and ALL 0, LOW_USAGE 3 (one game). The loader's game-cluster bootstrap is too narrow with 6 clusters, so t-intervals over game means (5 df) are given as the honest ones. (2) The close of 15 of 16 fills is 'captured': the app's own fair (CNO's books or Vigilant's line) read in the last minutes before the start, not Pinnacle; it matches the Tracker closes of Tj's taker bets (190 in the bid kinds) but not the study's Pinnacle/ESPN/Novig-trades closes; for the 11 no-sharp fills the fair and the close share a source family, which can flatter CLV. One close is Novig's last 8 trades (+9.5%). (3) The 300 unfilled bids are the NEWEST 300 only, in 3 bursts over 6 hours (18:06-18:09, 18:49-19:27, 22:26-00:05 ET), not a random draw of 3082; rates per bid-hour for older bids are derived by subtracting the sample from the app's 24-hour bid-hours (119.8) and are approximate. Led, distance and book age come from Novig's book read up to 507 s before posting (median 28 s). (4) Fill time is known for 6 fills; for 9 more the rest time is used (an upper bound by a few seconds); 2 partial fills have none. EV at fill is judged for 5 of 17. (5) The taker comparisons use the study's unit-stake listings at the first-listed price (not what Tj bet), mixed close sources, and 13 of the 17 bid sides are also in the study as Tj-placed rows. The 'if filled regardless' CLV assumes a fill is independent of the later drift and uses the listing's fair at first look, picked because it looked +EV for a taker (its drift is biased down). (6) Splits were run on about 12 variables; with 1-11 fills each none can be believed. Results (ROI) are noise at this size. Nothing here involves a bid rule being loosened; every change is a question for Tj.
key_numbers: 17 fills of 3128 bids posted in 14 days (0.54% per bid; 1 fill in the 927 bids older than 24 h, 16 in the last 24 h's 2201: Fisher p=0.032), all auto-make (0 of 94 by-hand bids filled), in only 6 games (7 fills in one game, 3 in another); $32.18 staked, mean $1.89 a fill (range $0.71-$2.74); 3 of the 17 filled only partly (144/585, 404/569, 344/518 contracts).

CLV of fills +2.57% on 16 closes in 6 games, beat the close 12 of 16 (75%); 95% interval over the 6 game clusters +0.80% to +4.34% (t, 5 df; the loader's bootstrap says +1.60% to +4.76% but is too narrow with only 6 clusters); positive in 6 of 6 games (exact sign-flip p=0.016 one-sided); excluding the one fill whose close is Novig's last 8 trades: +2.11% on 15 closes in 5 games (t-interval +0.92% to +3.30%). 15 of the 16 closes are 'captured' (the app's own fair read just before the start), not Pinnacle.

Both date halves positive: first 9 fills (Oct 3 - Oct 5 12:10) +3.31% on 8 closes, 5 games (t-interval -0.42% to +7.04%); last 8 fills (Oct 5 12:10 - 19:25) +1.83% on 8 closes, 4 games (-0.11% to +3.77%). Neither half alone is significant.

Results: 7 wins of 17, profit -$0.10 on $32.18 staked (ROI -0.3%, game-cluster 95% CI -54% to +79%); the CLV predicts about +$1.00 and 7.5 wins were expected at the prices, so nothing here is lucky or unlucky; results need about 6,700 bets to confirm a 2.6% edge at 2 SE.

The edge claimed at posting was +4.15% (16 with closes) and the close kept +2.57%: a giveback of 1.58 points (t-interval -0.01 to +3.17), the fair drifting -1.51% between posting and the close; the study's 495 taker listings in the same kinds (props, team totals; 39 games) gave back 1.73 points (EV +1.87% to CLV +0.13%; fair drift -1.70%, CI -2.28 to -1.05), so no adverse selection beyond the normal fair drift is visible.

Taking the same sides at Novig's price when the bids were posted would have averaged CLV -3.39% (t-interval -5.57% to -1.20%; 3 of 16 positive): the bids sat on average 2.65 cents (6.2%) under the offer, so making is the only route to an edge in those markets, not a cheaper route to the same one. 13 of the 17 sides were also listed in the study as taker bets: on the 11 with closes (4 games) the bid price beat the first-listed taker price by 3.29 points of CLV (t-interval +1.86 to +4.72) on the identical close.

Bids versus takers of the same kinds (props+team totals): bids +2.57% vs takers +0.13% (495 closes, 39 games; difference +2.44 pts, bootstrap 95% +1.21 to +4.52) or +0.60% on the like-for-like Tracker closes (190, 36 games; difference +1.97, +0.38 to +4.25); but against takers listed at EV 3% or more, the bid-sized edge, takers got +2.30% (93 closes, 30 games; difference +0.27 pts, -1.76 to +2.82). Per dollar a bid is as good as a +4% taker listing, not better; per bet a fill is $1.89 (expected CLV profit $0.049) against $1.75 for Tj's placed prop bets.

Fill rate: 0.134 fills per bid-hour in the last 24 h (16 in 119.8 bid-hours, Poisson 95% 0.076-0.217), against 19.2 expected by the app's research curve (observed/expected 0.83, P=0.28): bids fill about as the research said, they just rest only 2.4 min at the median (90th percentile 5.3 min), so a bid fills 0.54% of the time. Since Oct 5 18:06: LOW_USAGE 3 fills in 5.50 bid-hours (0.55/h, 0.11-1.6), QUICK_LIKELY 0 in 7.58 bid-hours (upper 95% 0.49/h; the curve expected 0.66, P(0)=0.52), the older all-kinds bids 13 in about 105.7 bid-hours (0.123/h).

Leading the book decides whether a bid fills: 16 of 17 fills led their side against 57% of the 3028 unfilled bids (binomial P=0.001, odds ratio 12); in the LOW_USAGE burst 3 of the 4 bids that led filled and 0 of 147 that did not (Fisher p=7e-6); 211 of the newest 303 bids sat behind a better bid (median 1 cent behind) and filled 0 times in 8.53 bid-hours. Fills were also nearer the offer: 2.65 cents under it (median 2.0) against 4.1 (median 4.0) for the 294 unfilled with a book (Mann-Whitney p=0.002). 79% of the 3082 unfilled bids ended by housekeeping (fair goes old 40.9%, expiry 37.8%), 2.7% because the fair fell.

The current QUICK_LIKELY setting has produced no fill and no information: its 116 bids (62 props, 54 team totals) were all posted 17.9 to 23.2 h before the start, a median 5.5 cents under the offer (LOW_USAGE: 2.5), and every one of the 17 fills was posted at most 8.5 h before the start (the trap guard's window is set to 24 h; its default is 6 h). Fills under rules like QUICK_LIKELY's (props/team totals, 0.444-0.60, sharp book in the fair): 4 fills in 2 games, CLV +1.94% (3 of 4 beat).

'Fast fill = stale bid' is not supported: 6 of 15 timed fills came within 2 minutes against 65% expected if bids are hit at a constant rate over the 2-3 minutes they rest (P(this few)=0.04); the 6 fast fills have CLV +4.13% (6 of 6 beat) against +1.13% for the 9 slower ones (5 of 9); all 5 fills the next scan could judge still had edge (EV at post +3.88%, at fill +3.79%, 0 picked off). The Diagnostics WARN 'most fills came within 2 minutes' fired on 3 of 6 (HealthChecks.kt line 146).

What a bid would earn if every one filled regardless of what the market did next (study listings in the bid kinds, price 0.30-0.60 after a 3.5% margin, first-look fair against the close): CLV +2.36% (472 closes, 39 games, 95% +1.71 to +3.02; both date halves +2.36 and +2.39); 6-24 h before the start +1.95% (313, 26 games) against 6 h or less +3.63% (151, 35 games); margin 2.5%: +1.39%, 4%: +2.85%. The actual fills (+2.57%) match it, so a bid keeps about margin minus 1.5 to 2 points.

Scale: expected CLV profit is about $0.05 a fill and $0.0065 a bid-hour; 17 fills in 14 days is $1.00 of expected edge. At 30-48 bids up (as in the QUICK_LIKELY burst) and 0.04-0.134 fills per bid-hour that would be 1.2-6.4 fills an hour while bids are up. Order-endpoint calls: 12,236 (/v3/orders 6,336 + /v3/orders/{id} 5,900) against about 2,955 auto bids posted over the same 4 days, about 4.1 per bid and about 720 per fill (includes 111 auto-bet orders). 13-45 wanted bids per pass (typically about 43) were waiting for the wallet or the day's limit while 22-32 rested in the QUICK_LIKELY burst, so capital, not eligibility, capped the bids up.

findings.claim: Filled bids beat the close: CLV +2.57% per fill
findings.evidence: 16 fills with a close, 6 games: mean +2.57%, 12 beat (75%), SD 3.73 pts; t-interval over 6 game clusters +0.80% to +4.34%; positive in all 6 games (game means +0.82%, +1.56%, +2.11%, +3.64%, +4.57%, +9.50%); exact sign-flip p=0.016; paired t on game means p=0.035; dropping any one game keeps it between +2.11% and +2.97%. 15 of 16 closes are 'captured' (the app's own CNO/Vigilant fair read in the last minutes), 1 is Novig's last 8 trades; 11 of the 17 fills were priced from a blend of soft books with no sharp book, so fair and close share a source family.
findings.effect: +2.57% (t-CI +0.80% to +4.34%; loader bootstrap +1.60% to +4.76%, too narrow for 6 clusters)
findings.luck_risk: about 2-4% that the true CLV is zero or negative given the 6 game-level signs (0.016 one-sided exact, 0.035 two-sided t); but 6 clusters, two rule eras, and the closes are the app's own fair: moderate. 14 of the 17 fills come from before the rules now in force.

findings.claim: The bids' results say nothing yet
findings.evidence: 7 wins of 17; profit -0.10 on 32.18 staked = ROI -0.3% (game-cluster CI -54% to +79%); expected from CLV +1.00; 7.5 wins expected at the prices; SD of total profit about 8.9. By group (all thin): PROP -9.51 on 19.62, TEAM_TOTAL +6.97 on 9.28, PERIOD +3.15, TOTAL -0.71; sharp-in-fair 6 fills -8.47 (1 win of 6; chance of 1 or fewer wins in 6 at about 50% is 11%) against no-sharp 11 fills +8.37.
findings.luck_risk: results are luck at this size: first half +6.97 (9 fills), second half -7.07 (8 fills); about 6,700 bets would confirm a 2.6% edge.

findings.claim: A filled bid gives back about 1.6 points of its claimed edge, the same as a taker listing: no extra adverse selection is visible
findings.evidence: EV at post +4.15% vs CLV +2.57% (16): giveback 1.58 pts (t-CI -0.01 to +3.17), fair drift post-to-close -1.51% (t-CI -3.02 to 0.00). Study taker listings, props+team totals: EV +1.87% vs CLV +0.13% (495 closes, 39 games) giveback 1.73; Tracker-closed 190: EV +1.99 vs CLV +0.60, giveback 1.38; listing fair drift -1.70% (CI -2.28 to -1.05). By margin: 2.5% -> CLV +1.56% (3 fills, 1 game), 3.0% -> +1.98% (3, 2 games), 4.0% -> +3.05% (10 closes, 5 games). Bias: the taker-listing drift is measured on rows picked because the fair looked high (winner's curse), so it overstates what a bid would give back; the bids' own fair at posting is not picked that way.
findings.effect: giveback 1.58 pts (t-CI -0.01 to +3.17); bids' drift -1.51% vs listings' -1.70% (CI -2.28 to -1.05)
findings.luck_risk: the equality of the two gives is an absence of evidence (6 games); adverse selection on fills cannot be measured without the close of the bids that did not fill

findings.claim: Making is not a cheaper way to the same edge; it is the only way to an edge where the taker price is not +EV, and per dollar it is no better than a +4% taker listing
findings.evidence: Taking at Novig's offer when each bid was posted: CLV -3.39% (t-CI -5.57% to -1.20%, 3 of 16 positive, 6 games); bid price on average 2.65 cents / 6.2% under the offer. Same-side pairs with the study's taker listing (13 of 17 sides listed, 11 with a close, 4 games; identical close): bid +3.29 pts better (t-CI +1.86 to +4.72); in 6 of 13 pairs the listing came after the bid and was 2.3% worse than the bid on average, 7 came before (5.8% worse); 2 of 13 listings were at or below the bid price. Takers in the same kinds: all closes +0.13% (495, 39 games), Tracker-closed +0.60% (190, 36 games), listed EV>=3% +2.30% (93, 30 games, Tracker-closed 46: +2.62%), listed EV 3-5% +1.36% (66, 26 games). Bid minus taker: +2.44 (+1.21, +4.52), +1.97 (+0.38, +4.25), +0.27 (-1.76, +2.82), +1.21 (-0.69, +3.94).
findings.effect: bid +2.57% vs takers at EV>=3% +2.30%: difference +0.27 pts (bootstrap 95% -1.76 to +2.82)
findings.luck_risk: the bid-vs-all-takers gap is real by construction (a 4% margin vs 1.9% listed EV); the bid-vs-EV>=3% takers difference is zero within +-2.5 pts. Pairs share the close, so only price differs; they are not a fill-probability comparison.

findings.claim: A bid's chance to fill is about 0.12-0.13 per bid-hour, as the research expected; bids simply rest only 2.4 minutes, so only 0.54% of them fill
findings.evidence: Last 24 h: 2201 bids, 119.8 bid-hours, 16 fills = 0.134/bid-hour (Poisson 95% 0.076-0.217); the app's research curve expected 19.2 (P(X<=16)=0.28). Rest time in the 303 newest bids median 2.37 min, 90th percentile 5.30 (app, all 3128: median 3, 90th 6). Before Oct 5 00:07: 1 fill in 927 bids (0.11%) against 16 in 2201 (0.73%) after: Fisher p=0.032. 17 / (3128 x 2.8 min = 146 bid-hours) = 0.117 per bid-hour over the whole 14 days (estimate).
findings.luck_risk: the expectation is the app's own curve, so agreement is weak evidence about the next window; 16 fills

findings.claim: Leading the book (and sitting within about 3 cents of the offer) is what makes a bid fill; most bids do not lead and never fill
findings.evidence: Fills: 16 of 17 led; unfilled: 57% of 3028 led (app) -> P(>=16 of 17 | 0.57)=0.001, Fisher odds ratio 12.1 (p=0.002). In the newest 303 bids (3 fills): bids that led 3 of 92 filled (5.62 bid-hours, 0.53 fills per bid-hour), bids behind a better bid 0 of 211 (8.53 bid-hours). In the LOW_USAGE burst (2.5% margin) only 4 of 151 bids led (the best bid sat 1-1.5 cents above the bid, spread 1 cent); 3 of the 4 filled, 0 of 147 others (Fisher p=7e-6). Cents under the offer: fills mean 2.65 / median 2.0; unfilled 294: mean 4.1 / median 4.0 (Mann-Whitney p=0.002); within LOW_USAGE all 3 fills were 2.0 cents or less under the offer against 17% of its unfilled. QUICK_LIKELY: 72 of 116 led but at a median 6.0 cents under the offer, 0 fills in 4.96 leading bid-hours (curve expected 0.44, P(0)=0.64). Leading and distance are confounded (only 3 fills): 3 of the 105 bids within 3 cents of the offer filled and 0 of 192 farther (Fisher p=0.043).
findings.effect: 3/92 led bids filled vs 0/211 behind (0.53 vs 0 fills per bid-hour); all-time 16/17 led vs 57%
findings.luck_risk: all-time led-share test P=0.001; LOW_USAGE burst p=7e-6 but all 3 fills are one game (ATL-NO) 17 minutes apart, so effectively one cluster: moderate. Era confound: the 57% comes from different versions.

findings.claim: The 'most fills came within 2 minutes = picked off' warning is a false alarm at this sample; fast fills did better, not worse
findings.evidence: 15 fills with a time (6 from fillDelaySec, 9 from rest time, an upper bound by seconds): median 2.23 min, 25%/75% 1.41/3.39, range 0.20-5.57. 6 of 15 (40%) within 2 min against 65.2% of bid-time lying in the first 2 min of a rest in the sample (constant-hazard expectation): P(X<=6)=0.04, so if anything fills come slightly later than a flat rate predicts. CLV: <=2 min +4.13% (6 fills, 5 games, 6 of 6 beat, drift +0.05%) vs >2 min +1.13% (9 fills, 4 games, 5 of 9 beat, drift -2.88%); Spearman rest-minutes vs CLV -0.47 (p=0.076, n=15). Fills in the first half of the bid's life +3.02% (6) vs second half +2.30% (10). EV at fill judged for 5 of 17 (the other 12 had no scan after the fill or pre-date the field): EV at post +3.88%, at fill +3.79%, fair moves +0.06%, -0.24%, 0, +0.65%, +0.34%, 0 picked off.
findings.effect: <=2 min +4.13% vs >2 min +1.13% (difference +3.0 pts, thin); 0 of 5 judged picked off
findings.luck_risk: the slow-fills-are-worse pattern is p=0.08: could be luck; it would fit adverse selection that grows with waiting

findings.claim: Why the newest bids did not fill: they were behind the book, far from the offer, short-lived and (for QUICK_LIKELY) posted overnight a day ahead
findings.evidence: The 300 newest unfilled (18:06-00:05 ET Oct 5-6, 3 bursts; with the 3 fills 303 bids): median 2.37 min rested (90th pct 5.30), 4.0 cents under the offer (294 with a book read) (LOW_USAGE 2.5, untagged 4.25, QUICK_LIKELY 5.5), 62 min to the start for LOW_USAGE vs 1233 for QUICK_LIKELY (all 116 between 1074 and 1390 min, 17.9-23.2 h), oldest sharp price a median 128 s old (newest 29.5 s), 70% (211 of 303) behind a better bid; the 303 bids were 135 distinct sides (2.2 posts per side; LOW_USAGE 3.6). End reasons in the sample: fair goes old within a minute 158 (LOW_USAGE 99 of 148 = 67%, all 36 untagged), about to expire 35, no longer a bid 45 (all LOW_USAGE), kill switch 32 and still resting 29 (QUICK_LIKELY). Across all 3082 unfilled: housekeeping re-posts 78.7%; only 2.7% (83) because the fair fell.
findings.luck_risk: a 6-hour sample of 3 bursts of the 3082 unfilled; not a random draw

findings.claim: Time to the start: the data points to 6 hours or less, but the 17 fills do not show it
findings.evidence: All 17 fills were posted 32-512 min (at most 8.5 h) before the start; 0 fills from 116 QUICK_LIKELY bids at 17.9-23.2 h (7.58 bid-hours; P(0)=0.52 even at the normal rate, so not proof). Actual fills <=6 h: 9 fills, 4 games, CLV +1.83%; 6-24 h: 8 fills, 3 games, CLV +3.52% (7 closes; margin 3.4% vs 3.7%): the reverse, thin. Study takers in the bid kinds, price 0.444-0.60: first look <=6 h CLV +1.67% (135 closes, 35 games, CI +1.15 to +2.49; ROI +10.5%) against 6-24 h -0.24% (273, 25 games, CI -1.21 to +0.68; ROI -2.4%): both halves agree in sign (H1 +1.58 vs -0.12; H2 +2.30 (17) vs -2.24 (15)). Hypothetical bid at 3.5% margin if filled: <=6 h +3.63% (151 closes, 35 games) vs 6-24 h +1.95% (313, 26 games); at 2.5% margin 6-24 h only +0.96% (CI +0.07 to +1.86). Tj's own placed bets: within 6 h +3.0% vs earlier -0.5% (app note, ScanSettings.kt STARTS_WITHIN_CHOICES). The code comment says 71% of prop takers' dollars trade in the last 6 h. trapEarlyHours defaults to 6 and is 24 now.
findings.effect: takers <=6 h +1.67% vs 6-24 h -0.24% (difference +1.9 pts); hypothetical bid +3.63% vs +1.95% (+1.7 pts); actual fills -1.7 pts (the other way, 7-9 fills)
findings.luck_risk: taker/hypothetical gap is across 25-35 games per band and holds in both halves; fill-level contradiction is 8 vs 9 fills: likely luck

findings.claim: Margin: a filled bid keeps about its margin minus 1.5 points, so 2.5% is a sensible floor and nothing below about 2% should be tried
findings.evidence: Margin 2.5% -> CLV +1.56% (3 fills, 1 game); 3.0% -> +1.98% (3, 2 games); 4.0% -> +3.05% (10 closes, 5 games); pooled slope of CLV on margin 1.02 (r=0.18, p=0.51, n=16: not significant). Hypothetical (study listings, if filled): 2.5% +1.39% (469 closes, 39 games, CI +0.75 to +2.03), 3.5% +2.36%, 4.0% +2.85%. Giveback 1.4-2.1 pts per margin cell; at 6-24 h the giveback is larger (drift -2.04% on study listings vs -0.40% within 6 h).
findings.luck_risk: model-based, not a result; the actual-fill slope is not significant

findings.claim: Kind, league, price band, sharp-in-fair, books, fair age: every split is too thin to say
findings.evidence: Kind: PROP +2.23% (10 closes, 3 games, 7 beat), TEAM_TOTAL +3.45% (4, 3 games, 4 of 4), PERIOD +9.50% (1), TOTAL -4.47% (1, a 0.165 longshot posted 8.5 h out). League: MLB +1.68% (9, 2 games), NHL +3.95% (3, 2), NFL +1.56% (3, 1), NCAAF +9.50% (1). Price: 0.40-0.50 +2.42% (9 closes, 6 games), 0.50-0.60 +4.87% (4, 3 games), 0.30-0.40 +2.19% (2), under 0.20 -4.47% (1). Sharp book in the fair: 6 fills +1.27% (3 games, 4 beat, -8.47 profit) vs none 10 closes +3.35% (5 games, 8 beat, +8.37): the reverse of what requiring a sharp book expects, with fair and close from the same consensus family for the no-sharp ones. Books behind the fair: 2 books +3.12% (7 fills), 3-4 +2.50% (4), 5+ +1.86% (5 closes). LOW_USAGE fair books: FanDuel+Kalshi 2 fills +0.8%, FanDuel+ProphetX 1 fill +3.0%; fair age 86/53/125 s oldest, 54/16/16 s newest, no pattern. Focus: untagged 14 fills +2.81% (13 closes, 5 games), LOW_USAGE 3 fills +1.56% (1 game), QUICK_LIKELY and ALL 0.
findings.effect: no split has more than 11 fills or 5 games
findings.luck_risk: with about 12 splits tried, one or two will look significant by chance; none is. About 55 fills per group are needed to see a 2-point difference.

findings.claim: Dollars: bids are a small, cheap addition; the fills so far are worth about $1 of expected edge in 14 days
findings.evidence: $1.89 a fill (median $1.99; 361-585 contracts a fill, mean 474), expected CLV profit $0.049 a fill, $0.0065 a bid-hour at 0.134 fills per bid-hour. 4.1 order-endpoint calls per bid posted, about 720 per fill. Bids are capped by the wallet or day limit, not by eligibility: 13-45 wanted bids waited per pass (typically about 43) while 22-32 rested (22:26-22:37 Oct 5). Novig answered /v3/orders with HTTP 451 (VPN/proxy screen) 145 times and DNS errors 13 times; reads of the open orders failed repeatedly between 19:33 (DNS x6) and 22:25 (HTTP 451 x8 from 20:21) on Oct 5, and the sample has no bids from 19:27 to 22:26.
findings.effect: about $0.05 expected CLV per fill; $0.0065 per bid-hour
findings.luck_risk: arithmetic from a +2.57% CLV whose interval is +0.8% to +4.3%: $0.015-$0.082 per fill

candidate_rules.name: taker, bid kinds, price 0.444-0.60, first look 6 h or less to start
candidate_rules.rationale: the population a QUICK_LIKELY bid competes in, near the start; bids earn a margin on top of this

candidate_rules.name: taker, bid kinds, price 0.444-0.60, first look 6-24 h to start
candidate_rules.rationale: the 6-24 h window the guard admits today (all 116 QUICK_LIKELY bids): takers lose to the close here, a bid needs its margin to cover the drift (-2.0%)

candidate_rules.name: taker, bid kinds, listed EV 3%+, within 24 h, price 0.30-0.60 (the edge a 3.5% bid claims)
candidate_rules.rationale: comparator for the bids at equal claimed EV: CLV +2.37% (91 closes, 29 games) against the bids' +2.57%; the second half has 7 closes

app_changes_implied: PROPOSAL (question for Tj; it tightens, so it is not a loosening, but it also changes the auto-bet and alerts): put the trap guard's window back from 24 h to its default 6 h (ScanSettings.trapEarlyHours, TrapGuard.DEFAULT_EARLY_HOURS = 6; bids read it as MakerRules.earlyHours, MakerQuote.kt) or to 12 h. Evidence: takers in the bid kinds at 0.444-0.60 +1.67% within 6 h (135 closes, 35 games) vs -0.24% at 6-24 h (273, 25 games); a bid with a 3.5% margin if filled +3.63% vs +1.95% (151 vs 313 closes); all 17 fills were at most 8.5 h out and the 116 QUICK_LIKELY bids at 18-23 h had 0 fills; the actual fills point the other way (+1.83%, 9 fills vs +3.52%, 8 fills), so it is not settled. About 30 fills in each band (60 fills, roughly 1-3 days at the QUICK_LIKELY pace if it fills at all) would settle it; to get them without changing the rule, keep the 24 h window for 2-3 more days and let the next file split fills by hours to start.

PROPOSAL (question for Tj; lowers the margin on the affected bids, so his decision): let a bid that sits 1-2 ticks behind the best bid step up to lead the book while it stays at least 2.0% under the fair (MakerQuote.kt: the price is PriceGrid.floor(fair / (1 + rules.margin)) near line 454; MakerRules.requoteSteps and the MakerPlan.PRIORITY order already treat leading as first). Evidence: 16 of 17 fills led (57% of unfilled did); in the LOW_USAGE burst 97% of bids (147 of 151) did not lead and filled 0 times while 3 of the 4 that led filled; a filled bid keeps about margin minus 1.5 pts, so 2.0% leaves about +0.5% per fill, 2.5% about +1.0%. Do not go under 2.0%. Settle it first without risking money: simulate it from Novig's public trades (tools/research/novig_bid_focus_study.py) and log would-lead prices; then about 100 fills per arm would separate +0.5% from +1.5%.

PROPOSAL (diagnostics only, no bet rule): change the 'most fills came within 2 minutes of posting' warning (app/HealthChecks.kt line 146: fast.size >= 6 and half under 120 s) to compare with the expected share under a constant fill rate (about 65% for bids that rest 2-3 minutes) and to need at least 20 timed fills; today it fired on 3 of 6 and the 6 fast fills had the best CLV (+4.13%).
